newsitem.title: UK: English China Clay slips after H1 results.
newsitem.headline: English China Clay slips after H1 results.

text.p: Shares in English China Clays Plc slipped in early trading on Monday after the company reported a tumble in first half profits for 1996, traders said.
Shares stood 6-1/2p down at 220p by 0750 GMT, in a generally buoyant market.

The company said its pretax profit was 5.7 million stg for the first half of 1996, compared with 55.3 million stg in the previous year. The drop was due to a fall in demand for minerals from the paper industry and a high level of costs "of a semi-fixed nature," it said.
"People are going to sit on the sidelines until we see physical signs of the paper cycle turning which we haven't seen yet," said Nick Wilson, diversified industrials analyst at Kleinwort Benson.
English China Clays said trading conditions since June had not been "significantly different from the first half". It said in the paper division, "the position is mixed, depending on market segment".
Wilson said although the interim dividend was being maintained at 5.5 pence per share, it was probably more of a defensive gesture than anything else.
In the U.S. and European operations, the company said it saw the need for further cost cutting following an ongoing strategic review.
